title: Potential influence of omega-3 fatty acids on PRP quality for use in orthopaedic sports medicine
summary:
An anti-inflammatory diet can significantly help to enhance the effectiveness of PRP therapy. To this end, the aim is to investigate the extent to which a 12-week course of supplementation with marine omega-3 fatty acids (EPA+DHA) demonstrably improves specific quality parameters of PRP.
To this end, participants with symptomatic osteoarthritis will be randomised within this study to either the intervention or control group. Both groups will undergo 
an initial assessment of PRP quality and individual systemic inflammation potential. The intervention group will subsequently receive a daily supplement of marine omega-3 fatty acids. 
The participants’ current diet is maintained in both groups, apart from the 
supplementation, and is assessed using standardised dietary questionnaires throughout the study. 
After 6 and 12 weeks, a further assessment of PRP quality and 
inflammatory potential is carried out in both groups. In addition, at the 
time points for measuring blood parameters, standardised questionnaires will be used to assess restricted mobility and pain perception. After week 
12, a one-way crossover will be carried out for the control group. The control group will now receive marine omega-3 fatty acid supplementation for a further 12 weeks. At 18 and 24 weeks, further measurements of PRP quality and inflammatory potential in the blood are carried out, and pain levels and restrictions in movement are assessed using standardised questionnaires.
conditions: Participants with symptomatic hip or knee osteoarthritis are included.

interventions.name:
Intervention group: 
- Duration of the study: 12 weeks
- Omega-3 oil supplementation over 12 weeks. 
- the daily dose of omega-3 oil is 4 grams
- Blood samples are taken and questionnaires are completed at the start of the study, after 6 weeks and after 12 weeks

Control group: 
- Study duration: 24 weeks (12-week control phase, followed by a 12-week intervention phase as part of a one-way crossover design)
- No intervention takes place during the first 12 weeks. Following the one-way crossover, omega-3 oil is taken for a further 12 weeks.
- Blood samples

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Participants with symptomatic osteoarthritis of the knee or hip   
• Presence of an indication for PRP therapy
Exclusion criteria:
• Existing regular omega-3 supplementation within the last 6 
months 
• Contraindications to PRP therapy, such as: 
  - A previously diagnosed coagulation disorder  
  - Use of anticoagulants (with the exception of ASS-100) 
  - Acute infections 
  - Active malignant diseases 
• To minimise the risk, individuals at increased risk of atrial fibrillation 
are excluded, in particular: 
  - known atrial fibrillation or other relevant supraventricular arrhythmias 
  - known relevant structural heart disease 
  - known, recent cardiovascular events 
  - known QT prolongation or relevant rhythm disturbances
